parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminal offence, facility/custody regime, border-document practice or trans violence rate is documented, so the same-sex statute is treated as secondary, not dominant. It still matters through documented surroundings: Article 354 allows 3 months-2 years if a trans visitor's conduct or relationship is read as same-sex, Art. 360 covers minors, police/prosecutors refuse to investigate crimes against LGBTQ+ people, there is no anti-discrimination protection, and official and social framing is hostile with 15% viewing the area as good for gay/lesbian people. That thin recourse plus hostile threat-framing places the case in High Risk, above routine custodial abuse but below administrative-only regimes.

entry_documents.exposure: No documented rejection of foreign passports or X markers. No domestic marker-change pathway is a resident gap, not documented visitor exposure.
entry_documents.interaction: Foreign documents would reach checkpoints whose treatment of mismatch is not documented.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Art. 354: 3 months-2 years for consensual same-sex adult conduct, applicable if trans visitor is read as same-sex. Art. 360: 1-3 years for same-sex sexual contact with a minor.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: 2013 wedding sentences were suspended on appeal; no capital penalty for this conduct is documented.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A male partner or a minor companion could make the same-sex reading more likely; post-2017 enforcement frequency is not documented.

care_services.exposure: Healthcare discrimination and hostility are documented for LGBTQ+ people; no formal blood-donation ban is documented.
care_services.interaction: Hostile access could delay care after outing, but no ward-placement or medication rule is documented.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Official hostility is on record; a former prime minister defended criminalisation religiously. LGBTQ+ people are framed socially as threats to family and procreation.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: No formal restriction on expression, association or assembly is documented; Art. 350(i) punishes rape motivated by sexual orientation with 10-20 years.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Threat-framing supports the criminal statute's social licence, while Art. 350(i)'s application is undocumented.

minors_guardians.exposure: Art. 360 creates 1-3 years' exposure only if a sexual relationship/touching with a same-sex minor is alleged; mere travelling with a minor is not documented as an offence.
minors_guardians.interaction: An adult guardian read as same-sex in relation to a minor faces greater charging exposure than a solo adult, but no family-detention practice is documented.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Police and prosecutors refuse to investigate or prosecute crimes against LGBTQ+ people. People hide their identity for safety; 2024 survey: 15% say local area is good for gay/lesbian people.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Art. 350(i) provides 10-20 years for bias-motivated rape, but whether it has been applied is not stated.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Hostility plus documented non-investigation removes realistic recourse if outed, even without trans-specific violence statistics, which are absent.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No general anti-discrimination protection. Uncorroborated claims of dozens imprisoned under pretext are deliberately not counted. Current enforcement frequency and trans-specific violence are undocumented.
remedies_unknowns.protection: The 2013 suspended sentences show appeal/community outcry once worked, but this is dated and pre-dates the 2017 code.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Absence of current data is not safety; extrapolation uses criminalisation, no recourse and hostile climate.

anchor_checks.comparison: Higher than 0.15: no documented routine arrest for presentation, months-long pretrial abuse, beatings, or capital risk. Imprisonment is legally possible under Art. 354, but routine custodial torture is not documented.

Lower than 0.35: that anchor involves exclusion/humiliation without credible imprisonment. Here imprisonment is authorised, police refuse LGBTQ+ crime investigations, and hostility is documented, so consequences after outing are more severe despite less universal border exposure.

Well below 0.55: that case is administrative delay and denial of entry with working appeals. Here criminalisation, official hostility, hostile social framing and documented refusal to investigate crimes leave no comparable working remedy.

parsed.synthesis: The combined regime is criminalisation on the books plus documented non-protection in practice. A trans visitor is not shown to face a trans-specific offence, facility ban, custody placement or border-document regime, which prevents a Severe rating. But if outed and read as same-sex, especially with a partner or minor, Article 354/360 allow imprisonment, while police non-investigation and hostile threat-framing mean the traveller has little recourse. The single bias-rape provision and the dated 2013 suspended sentences do not offset that operative reality.
